(You are all considered "trained" for this exercise, so you don't need to roll intelligence checks to use your stations)

Pilot - (Dexterity or Wisdom)
All Pilots add either their dexterity or wisdom modifiers to pilot skill checks. 
Must be in a functional pilot station.
“Untrained” Pilots must pass a DC20 Intelligence check before attempting to take a pilot action. Critical failure disables the station.
“Trained” Pilots add their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking pilot actions. 
“Ace” Pilots add double their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking pilot actions. 

Action: Weather Gage. Choose one other ship in your zone. Make a pilot check DC20 to gain advantage on attack rolls against that ship until the end of your ship’s turn. This applies to all crew members and includes personal attack rolls. You can have the weather gage on more than one other ship at a time.
Action: Close the Distance. Move toward target aircraft in the same zone. Make a pilot check DC10 to bring ships within “Close Range” (allows Boarding, Bombing, and Personal attacks, range of 10-30’). After your ship’s turn ends, you are no longer at “Close Range”. As part of this action, you can choose to Ram the enemy ship causing 3d10 bludgeoning damage to both ships as if hit.
Action: Full ahead. Move into adjacent zone. DC 5
Reaction: Swerve. Pass a Pilot check DC 20 to cause one attack roll against your ship to fail.

Gunner - (Strength or Intelligence) 
All Gunners add either their Strength or Intelligence modifiers to Gunner skill checks. 
Must be in a functional Artillery or Bombing station.
“Untrained” Gunners must pass a DC20 Intelligence check before attempting to take a Gunner action. Critical failure disables the station.
“Trained” Gunners add their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking gunner actions. 
“Ace” Gunners add double their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking gunner actions. 

Action: Barrage. Use your Gunner skill check result as an attack roll to fire upon other ships using “artillery” or “bombing” stations. Personal bonuses to attack rolls do not apply.
Bonus Action: Load special ammunition

Mechanic - (Dexterity or Intelligence)
All Mechanics add either their Dexterity or Intelligence modifiers to Mechanic skill checks. 
No station required.
“Untrained” Mechanics must pass a DC20 Intelligence check before attempting to take a Mechanic action. Critical failure causes 10 damage to the hull.
“Trained” Mechanics add their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking Mechanic actions. 
“Ace” Mechanics add double their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking Mechanic actions. 
Action: Repair Hull. Roll a Mechanic check DC20. Restore 10 hit points to hull. If airship is equipped with a Repair Bay, DC is 10.
Action: Jury Rig. Roll a Mechanic check DC10. A disabled station becomes functional again. This does not restore hit points.
Bonus action: Overcharge. Mechanic can give a boon to other stations. This lasts until the start of the mechanics next turn. The mechanic can overcharge an active station in the following ways.
Engine Overcharge - Roll a Mechanic check DC5. On failure, the engine is disabled. On success, Pilot gains one additional pilot action. This extra pilot action can be used until the start of the mechanic’s next turn.
Munitions Overcharge - Increase the damage one weapons station can deal by 1d10. This extra damage lasts until the start of the mechanic’s next turn.
Hasty Repair - Roll a Mechanic check DC15. On a success, you restore 10 points to hull. On failure, hull takes 10 damage.

Captain - (Constitution, Charisma)
All Captains add either their Constitution or Charisma modifiers to Captain skill checks. 
No station required.
“Untrained” Captains have no penalty to take a Captain action. Anyone can be captain!
“Trained” Captains add their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking Captain actions. 
“Ace” Captains add double their proficiency bonus to rolls made when taking Captain Actions. 
Free Action: Decides crew initiative order at the start of each round.
Action: Activate special ability, like cloak, ethereal jaunt, teleport, summon creature, or mend if available.
Action: Spyglass. The spyglass action can be used in one of three ways. Make a Captain skill check DC 10. On success:
1. Learn the current hit point value of one ship in the battle. 
2. Learn what stations one target ship has, and which are disabled. 
3. One ship in cloud cover is revealed for the rest of your ship’s turn. Their location is lost as soon as the ship’s turn ends. 
Reaction: Inspire. Give one crew member advantage on next ship action requiring a d20 roll, including untrained crew.
Reaction: Called shot. When your ship attacks successfully, before damage is rolled, name a station on your opponent’s ship. That station gains vulnerability to damage from this attack.
